source.title: Gradient Flow in Sparse Neural Networks and How Lottery Tickets Win
source.authors: Utku Evci; Yani Ioannou; Cem Keskin; Y. Dauphin

record.file_problem: none; full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests sparsity-aware initialization and gradient flow in sparse networks, extending initialization findings to unstructured sparse models. Its reported outcomes do not test training classification error, shortcut effects, learning-rate stability, or batch-normalization speed.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy and gradient-flow results for sparse training, but no training classification-error results. Its test-accuracy figures and tables are not rows for the listed versions because those versions concern training error, learning speed, trainable depth, or batch-normalization speed. The cited results from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study extends V4 to unstructured sparse networks: initialization affects vanishing gradients and the onset of learning in LeNet5 and VGG16. Appendix C also explicitly compares learning onset under He and Glorot initialization. It does not test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors conclude that naive sparse initialization causes poor gradient flow, per-neuron sparsity-aware initialization remedies the initial problem, and dynamic sparse training improves early gradient flow. They also conclude that lottery tickets succeed by relearning their originating pruning solution, limiting their ability to find diverse solutions and improve ensembles.
record.recipe_differences: Studies unstructured sparse networks and proposes initialization based on each neuron's connectivity; measures gradient flow and reports generalization, rather than testing the listed dense-network training-error claims.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization method changes gradient flow and the reported iteration at which learning begins; architecture and dataset differ across the reported settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Lottery tickets converge to solutions close to their originating pruning solution, with low prediction disagreement and limited ensemble gains.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lottery-ticket success can arise from relearning the originating pruning solution rather than improved gradient flow.

fits_no_version.finding: Dynamic connectivity updates improve gradient flow and change the Hessian spectrum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dynamic sparse connectivity can improve early optimization; these results do not establish initialization effects or learning-rate stability thresholds.

record.problems: The relevant gradient-flow curves are figures without reported numeric values or uncertainty in the text. The paper reports test accuracy, not training classification error, for the sparse-model outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1, Table 2, and Table 6 report test accuracy/generalization rather than the behaviors named by the listed versions. Figure 3 and related Hessian results concern dynamic sparse connectivity updates rather than initialization effects named by V4.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, and model-size or training-recipe qualifications.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious local minima, and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation across depth, identity-shortcut comparisons, deep plain tanh networks, and Fixup.

Greater trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization; very deep tanh networks and 10,000-layer convolutional networks. ResNet-50 gradient-flow results do not establish a learning-speed effect.
Stability thresholds, catapult recovery, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence below or above thresholds.
Controlled batch-normalization comparisons for training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training without normalization.

missing.what: Learning starts faster for Scratch LeNet5 with He initialization than with Glorot initialization; record the initialization comparison and qualitative learning-onset result.

record.verdict_notes: Final test accuracy is not training classification error or training speed. In particular, unchanged ResNet-50 test accuracy does not challenge V4. Neither gradient-flow improvements alone nor lottery-ticket convergence establish the full initialization-and-depth claim.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels, and effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual networks across depth, and the effects of normalization or Fixup on training error.

The study tests sparsity-aware initialization and gradient flow in sparse models. It does not test activation-matched initialization in plain dense networks, trainable depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, or 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning rates above the stability limit, loss recovery, sharpness, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effect on accuracy speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup without normalization.

rows.subject: LeNet5
rows.operation_detail: Measured gradient flow during training with dense-model initialization in a sparse network.
rows.measure: Training gradient flow; the text reports when learning starts.
rows.note: The authors state that dense-initialized sparse LeNet5 starts learning after 1000 iterations; this measures sparse-network learning progress, not classification error.
rows.check: The reported 1000-iteration delay is correct. This is evidence of delayed learning under mismatched initialization, rather than a partial occurrence of V4. Interpret alongside the sparsity-aware comparison in R3.

rows.subject: LeNet5, VGG16, and ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Measured gradient flow during training with the proposed sparsity-aware initialization.

conditions.value: MNIST for LeNet5; ImageNet-2012 for VGG16 and ResNet-50

rows.value: Figure only; authors state the proposed initialization remedies vanishing gradient at initialization.
rows.note: The paper states this initialization remedies vanishing gradient at initialization and shows gradient flow curves; it does not give numeric gradient-flow values in the text.
rows.check: The stated remedy of vanishing gradients is supported, but split this aggregate into architecture-specific rows: LeNet5 at 95% sparsity and VGG16 and ResNet-50 at 80%. For ResNet-50 the text reports only some initial gradient-flow improvement; it does not establish faster learning or greater trainable depth. Gradient improvement alone must not be presented as a measured training-speed gain.

relationships.condition: 95% sparse LeNet5 on MNIST and 80% sparse VGG16 on ImageNet, comparing masked dense initialization with sparsity-aware initialization
relationships.reason: R1–R2 report delayed learning under masked dense initialization; R3 and §4.1 report that sparsity-aware initialization remedies the initial vanishing gradients. This supports the initialization and early-learning component in these sparse settings.
relationships.display_finding: Masked dense initialization delayed learning, while sparsity-aware initialization remedied initial vanishing gradients.
